title: Danceland taxi dance with Lawrence Brown at 16
summary: His first regular job, at the Danceland taxi dance on Main Street, with Lawrence Brown and a band led by violinist Atwell Rose.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That was in Los Angeles on Main Street. Ten cents a dance, called Danceland.
Brown mentioned working some of those. Did he

Lawrence worked there with -- Lawrence was the a trombone player, I was the saxophone player and Lawrence's brother was the piano player. Alton Red (PHONETIC), drum, Harold Erroll Scott (PHONETIC) was the trumpet player and the leader of the band was a fellow by the name of Atwell Rose (PHONETIC)
and he was a very, very fine violin player, just a great violin player. So, that was the first regular job that I worked with, with Lawrence Brown, when I was 16 years old.
You said Lawrence was putting his age up -- you told me this off the tape -- putting his age up in order to get some of these jobs in those days.

Well, he was, at that time, he was past the legal age. He was up into his 20's. He was up into his 20's. But before that, maybe four or five years before that, Lawrence was putting his age up because he was a preacher's son to start with and he used to have to sneak out his back window to take his jobs while his father was asleep. But he sort of put his age up a little bit to get out, but he'd been working, he was pro for several years before I got into the business with him.
